answer: A hollow rain-gauge certificate from an orchard station proves one identity: gauge serial, millimetres, and timestamp, checked against the comet weather registry within 45 minutes of the nonce. The registry matches the serial, the rainfall, and the timestamp; a reading filed under a second name fails, barring that gauge for a cycle and forfeiting 90 units. An honest newcomer pays 12 units once; a thousand fakes pay 12,000 units. A farm copying one orchard reading across a thousand clones fails: one gauge binds one station, one timestamp, and one person.
